body.rationale: IPS status: ratified, as the brief states. The reviews also treat the breaches as real. I ranked for portfolios the CIO can build from under the IPS, favouring covariance-based methods over return-forecast methods, as the late-cycle finding in §4.3 suggests. I did not rank myself. Inverse variance breaches the volatility floor (6.94%), and my own reviewers found errors in my write-up. 1) inverse_volatility: no hard breaches, eff. N 14.8, and no return forecast reaches the weights. The reviewers' only criticism was the correlated credit cluster of about 43%, plus a minor 'equal-risk-style' wording issue. 2) resampled_efficient_frontier: no breaches and broad (eff. N 13.1), so resampling does tame the optimiser. Its drawdown of -24.84% leaves little headroom against the -25% limit, which the BL reviewer flagged, so it is second. 3) cvar_minimization: no breaches and the best drawdown among compliant methods (-18.7%), with a different tail-aware lens. It is concentrated (eff. N 2.9) and its volatility is tuned exactly to the 8% floor, per the tail_risk_parity review. 4) risk_parity: a covariance-only method adding risk-structured diversity. It breaches the volatility floor only mildly (7.56%). The reviews noted that its eff. N measures capital rather than risk, and that its 'no forecast' framing is an implicit forecast. 5) black_litterman: compliant, with a good backtest Sharpe, but its equilibrium prior double-counts overlapping ETF AUM and its drawdown headroom is only about 3 points. Why first beats fifth: inverse_volatility has no forecast dependence, no tuning and broader diversification (14.8 vs 5.7 eff. N), with a shallower hit to its drawdown limit (-22.9% vs -21.9% is similar, but BL's reliance on a distorted prior and tuned gamma adds estimation risk that inverse_volatility lacks). Flag: market_cap_weight. It has a -40.6% backtest drawdown (15.6 points beyond the limit), CRO risk 0.80, and about 77% equity. Its 'market portfolio' is ETF AUM, which the MCW reviewer says double-counts overlapping style funds. It describes itself as a diagnostic, so the CIO should not lean on it. I did not flag the adversarial diversifier, since its orthogonality is an ensemble feature, though I did not rank it either, because it breaches return, volatility and tracking error.
